content:
Apple today unveiled its latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models, while also making a small update to its Magic Keyboard accessories.

The new Magic Keyboard removes the text labels on the keys and replaces them with icons.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio are equipped with next-generation M6 and high-end M5 Ultra chips, delivering significant performance improvements.

The new models are now available for pre-order: Mac mini available here, Mac Studio available here.

In addition to the desktop computer improvements, Apple has also updated its Magic Keyboard lineup, with a minor change on the new models.

The new Magic Keyboard drops text labels on multiple keys in favour of icons.

Apple previously made the same change on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and the Magic Keyboard has now received the same update.

The change applies to all new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: US$99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: US$149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: US$179

Commonly used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift, and Delete have dropped text labels and now only display icons. On the extended models with numeric keypads, the Home, Page Up, and Page Down keys use brand-new icons to replace text.

The most-liked comment was posted by Caesarrr

I really don't understand this move. You know it causes inconvenience for users, so what benefit is worth sacrificing the user experience?

Apart from the switch to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks identical to the previous generation in every other respect, with the same USB-C support, features, and layout.

If you'd like to order the new Magic Keyboard from Amazon rather than from Apple, you can get them here: Magic Keyboard, the version with Touch ID, and the version with Touch ID and numeric keypad (in black).

What do you think about dropping the key text labels? Share your thoughts in the comments section.
